title: The spoon
logline: Monday of the kept week. The spoon. Fourteen times. The strip is a grid of spoons and Gully's face at the end of it.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD on the stool, drawing. BARNABY in the basket on the counter. GULLY.

balloons.text: The consommé spoon. Not a soup spoon. Deeper bowl. Shorter handle. Silver, not plate — you could tell by the weight —

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man drawing on a bait-shop stool while explaining something, an old dog in a basket on the counter, a stocky man in an apron

panels.composition: The pad: a spoon. Drawn perfectly. Beside it: another. Another.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a pad with several precise ink drawings of the same spoon

panels.composition: The pad, full: fourteen spoons in a grid. Every one exact. Every one the same.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a drawing pad filled with a grid of fourteen identical precise ink drawings of a spoon

panels.composition: Gully, looking at the pad. Then at Wood. Then at the dog, who is asleep.

balloons.text: You've drawn a spoon fourteen times.
It was a very good spoon.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a stocky man in an apron looking at a pad full of spoons then at the thin man who drew them

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Fourteen spoons. 'It was a very good spoon.'
